title: Wake-on-LAN
desc: Send Wake-on-LAN magic packets to devices on your LAN to power them on remotely
empty: No devices yet. Add one, or import a Lucky config under "Settings → Backup & Migration"
broadcastPlaceholder: Leave empty for auto; separate multiple with commas, e.g. 192.168.1.255
checkHelp: Periodically opens a TCP connection to this address to check whether the device is online
noConnections: No SSH connections in Web Terminal yet
untrustedHelp: Remote shutdown does not trust unknown hosts. Connect to this host once in Web Terminal to record its host key
shutdownHelp: Runs over the Web Terminal SSH connection. Windows needs the OpenSSH server enabled; on Linux, non-root users can use sudo -n shutdown -h now with passwordless sudo for that command.
bemfaTopicHelp: Requires Bemfa to be enabled. "Turn on" from a voice assistant wakes the device, "turn off" shuts it down (if remote shutdown is set up)
bemfaStep1: In the Bemfa console, create a topic under MQTT device cloud whose name ends with 001 (socket) or 006 (switch), e.g. pc001;
bemfaStep2: Enter the same topic on the device, then enter your private key here and enable it;
bemfaStep3: Link your Bemfa account in Mi Home (Xiao AI), Xiaodu or Google Home and sync devices to control them by voice.
bemfaUidPlaceholder: User private key from the Bemfa console
bemfaUidHelp: The private key works like an account credential; Gately only sends it over TLS to bemfa.com:9503
modeAgentDesc: Install an agent on the device; it connects to Gately on its own and supports shutdown, reboot and sleep. Works on Windows, Linux, macOS and OpenWrt, and the device does not need to expose any port
modeSSHDesc: Runs a shutdown command over an SSH connection in Web Terminal; the device needs its SSH service enabled
modeHTTPDesc: Sends an HTTP request, e.g. to the API of Home Assistant, a smart plug or a shutdown tool on the device
agentSaveHint: After saving, install commands for each system are shown; run one on the device
agentEditHint: Install commands and connection status are in "Agent" on the device card
agentServerHelp: The address the device uses to reach the Gately admin backend. Defaults to the current browser address and must be reachable from the device
agentServerInvalid: The address must start with http:// or https:// and may only contain letters, digits and characters such as :/._~%{'@'}-
agentGateway: You are currently accessing through the fnOS gateway, which devices cannot connect through. Enter Gately's direct address (e.g. http://NAS address:16601)
agentHttpWarn: HTTP addresses send the token in plain text; use HTTPS or limit this to the LAN
agentInsecureHelp: Enable when Gately uses a self-signed certificate; LAN use only
agentRegenerateConfirm: After regenerating, the old agent stops working immediately and must be reinstalled on the device with the new command. Continue?
agentRegenerated: Token regenerated. Please reinstall on the device
agentNoCommand: Enter a valid Gately address first
agentHelpWindows: Run in a PowerShell opened with "Run as administrator". The agent runs as a startup scheduled task under the SYSTEM account; the log is at C:\ProgramData\GatelyAgent\agent.log
agentHelpLinux: Run in a terminal (requires sudo and curl or wget). Installed as a systemd or OpenRC service that starts at boot
agentHelpMacos: Run in a terminal; the administrator password is required. Installed as a launchd daemon; the log is at /var/log/gately-agent.log. After sleep, Wake for network access must be enabled to wake it remotely
agentHelpOpenwrt: Run as root over SSH. Installed as a procd service and uses curl or the built-in wget
agentNote: The agent only performs shutdown, reboot and sleep, and Gately cannot make it run any other command. The token works like the power switch of this device, so keep it secret; one token can be used for one device only.
httpHelp: A 2xx response status counts as success. With method "Auto", POST is used when there is a body, otherwise GET
httpHeadersHelp: Put credentials (such as Authorization: Bearer …) in headers; read-only accounts cannot see their values
httpInsecureHelp: Enable when the target uses a self-signed certificate; LAN devices only
